The tensile strength exceeds 300 MPa even in alloy No. 1, in which the precipitation hardening phase is absent. This shows that the degree of dispersion strengthening of the Mn intermetallic phase is very large.

Through a combination of dispersion strengthening of the Q phase and precipitation hardening of the GPB zone, the strength of the P/M Al-3.6Mn-6.4Cu-3.6Zn-1.7Mg alloy (mass%) at 523 K was improved to 319 MPa with sufficient ductility.

Through a combination of dispersion strengthening of the Q phase and precipitation hardening of the GPB zone, the strength of the P/M Al-3.6Mn-6.4Cu-3.6Zn-1.7Mg alloy (mass%) at 523 K was improved to 319 MPa with sufficient ductility.
This indicates that the large decrease in tensile strength at 573 K is attributable to the decrease in the degree of precipitation hardening due to the dissolution of the GPB zone.
The hardness of alloy No. 3 always shows a hardness that is 15 HV higher than that of No. 2 alloy at any given aging condition.
